fields.claim_quote: \paren {j + 2} \paren {r - j + 2} \dbinom r {j + 2} \paren {\paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} \dbinom s {n - j} + \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} } }
fields.explanation:
Induction paragraph explicitly imposesj≥1. The packet headline r=2,j=0 misses that condition; complete neighboring expressions must also have a nonzero unchanged bracket. Use r=s=n=3,j=1, already among the original suggested alternatives. Source induction premise holds; bracket=3, complete sides9 and36. Actual Nat.choose and signed integer bracket preserve subtraction; replacement satisfiesj≥1 and all binomial ranges.

For r>=j+2, the adjacent-binomial identity (j+2) C(r,j+2)=(r-j-1) C(r,j+1) gives C(r,j+1)=[(j+2)/(r-j-1)] C(r,j+2). The denominator is positive in this domain. Multiplying this true identity by the unchanged bracket repairs that local transition.
fields.flaw: In the induction step, the transition from line 0052 to line 0055 (justified by 'Corollary: Factors of Binomial Coefficient 2') asserts the identity C(r, j+1) = (j+2)(r-j+2) C(r, j+2), i.e. it replaces the factor \dbinom r {j+1} by \paren{j+2}\paren{r-j+2}\dbinom r {j+2} while leaving the bracketed sum unchanged. This local equality is false.
fields.problem:
Title: Summation from k to m of r Choose k by s Choose n-k by nr-(r+s)k

:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {m + 1} \paren {n - m} \dbinom r {m + 1} \dbinom s {n - m}$
fields.witness: Take r=s=n=3 and j=1. The induction hypothesis holds atj=1; the unchanged bracket is3, and the two complete adjacent source expressions are9 and36. Thus the very same claimed line transition is false, withj≥1 and all binomialindices inrange.
